A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same INR classifier attack study despite the changed title and format. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original adversarial classification experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and ModelNet10, activation and latent-space analyses, and computational measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains the original empirical results and adds AutoAttack accuracy, BPDA robustness and comparative runtime measurements in Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: The five original attacks—Full PGD, TMO, BOTTOM, ICOP and implicit differentiation—and BVA are retained. Expanded threat-model explanations and newly disclosed implementation details do not establish procedural changes to these methods. AutoAttack and BPDA enter as additional evaluations; the implicit-gradient formula correction is addressed under T1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and voxelized ModelNet10 classification under the same image and voxel perturbation domains. AutoAttack and BPDA extend testing on existing data without introducing new datasets, populations, modalities or task requirements.

E2.justification: V3 adds AutoAttack to the MNIST/Fashion-MNIST accuracy comparison in Table 1 and evaluates BPDA in Table 2. Table 3 also compares AutoAttack component timings with the proposed attacks. The existing ViT, CNN, autoencoder and voxel-classifier baselines remain.

E3.justification: V3 extends the evaluation design with BPDA's identity approximation for the backward derivative of the INR optimization mapping and sequential AutoAttack testing. Section 4.5 introduces cumulative component-runtime comparisons against 100-step suite attacks. These are new testing procedures; the previously stated training, preprocessing and perturbation-budget settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.4.2 adds a diagnostic BPDA experiment testing whether apparent robustness survives bypassing gradient masking. Section 4.5 adds a detailed AutoAttack efficiency comparison. The existing activation-amplification, attack-bound sensitivity and latent-space analyses remain; moving Figure 6 into the main text does not constitute a new analysis.

E5.justification: V3 specifies five random restarts for the new BPDA evaluation, adding randomized repetition information absent from v1. These are attack restarts, not reported independent training runs or uncertainty estimates. No new confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced, and the existing shaded amplification plots are retained.

E6.justification: The original Table 1 scores and ModelNet10 table values are unchanged. New results include AutoAttack accuracies of 0.44 and 0.05, and BPDA accuracies of 0.076 and 0.159, for MNIST and Fashion-MNIST respectively at a 32/256 bound, plus Table 3 timings. V1 Appendix B.1.1's autoencoder accuracies of 98.8% clean and 11.28% robust are omitted.

T1.justification: V3 Section 3.4.5 adds a Taylor-expansion derivation and an explicit Hessian-invertibility assumption. Equation 5 corrects the inverse-Hessian and mixed-derivative multiplication order shown in v1 Equation 3. This is a localized mathematical correction and expansion of the existing implicit-differentiation analysis; Section 4.4 supplies empirical reasoning rather than a new robustness theorem.

C1.justification: V1's abstract and conclusion emphasize inherent adversarial robustness without robust training. V3 reframes the contribution as a security analysis, narrows the abstract's robustness claim to standard white-box attacks, attributes the behavior to gradient obfuscation, and makes vulnerability under alternative attacks an explicit contribution.

C2.justification: V1 already discusses attenuation and vanishing gradients, but v3 interprets the new attack failures as evidence of gradient masking rather than general security. It adds a spectral-bias/low-pass scrubbing hypothesis and explains implicit differentiation's fixed-point versus finite-trajectory mismatch. Applicability limitations are revised, while the conclusion's explicit clean-accuracy tradeoff is dropped.

D1.justification: V3 replaces the promise of future code release with a repository location and an availability statement. It newly documents L2 gradient clipping at 1, damped inverse-Hessian calculations, and classifier depths in the runtime discussion. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish that the retained experiments changed accordingly.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially beyond weight-space learning to gradient obfuscation, equilibrium models and adversarial purification. V3 positions the work against Athalye et al., Yang et al., DiffPure and robustness-trained INRs from Luo et al., while adding AutoAttack references and newer neural-functional learning work. This materially changes the security context and novelty positioning.

P1.justification: V3 retitles the paper and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, implicit-differentiation explanation and discussion. It introduces dedicated threat-model and mechanism sections, consolidates the conclusion and limitations, and relocates much of the computational analysis to Appendix C. These constitute substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with widespread figure resizing and relocation. Figure 1 replaces duplicated parameter-space panels with the intended parameter-versus-signal-space comparison. Table 1 gains AutoAttack columns, new BPDA and runtime tables appear, and Figure 6 moves from the appendix into the main text. Figures 2–10 otherwise retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: V1's central robustness claim relied on its proposed attack suite. V3 adds AutoAttack and especially BPDA results exposing severe vulnerabilities, then narrows the abstract's claim and explicitly identifies gradient masking. This substantially improves the evidence underlying the paper's central security assessment, supported by the corrected derivation and additional reproducibility information. The discussion still mislabels BPDA as gradient-free despite defining a gradient approximation, and retains some overbroad robustness wording, so the improvement does not resolve every interpretive problem.
